description.narrative: Genomförande av konferensen Africa Drive for Democracy - med målsättning av främja panafrikansk solidaritet och förnyat engagemang för demokrati
Support to the conference Africa Drive for Democracy 2023 - with the aim of forging Panafrican solidarity and renewed collaboration for democracy

The first Africa Drive for Democracy Conference (D4DC 2022) was convened in July 2022 in Arusha, Tanzania, under the theme 'Fighting the democratic backslide through renewed action and solidarity'. It was supported and initiated by the Swedish Embassy in Dar es Salaam as part of the Swedish Drive for Democracy campaign. The purpose was to provide a platform for networking and a renewed engagement for democratic progress on the continent. A consortium consisting of the Centre for Strategic Litigation (CSL), the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) and of the MS training Centre for Development Cooperation (MS TCDC) organised the conference with funding from the regional section at the Embassy in Addis Abeba. 120 participants from 29 countries participated. As an outcome of the first conference, the 'Africa Drive for Democracy Network' was launched with the aim to provide similar meeting places on an annual basis, and to establish a permanent structure. The Embassy decided to enter into an agreement with CSL to organize the second conference in July 2023 to meet the following three main objectives: i. To critically review and assess the state of the African democratic movement. ii. To identify, recognize and celebrate ongoing efforts on the continent towards building a strong democratic movement. iii. To deliberate on the opportunities for reviving solidarity and renewing the African democratic movement.

The conference is assessed to have been a relevant forum for learning, exchange and networking among the democratic community in Africa, but the success rate in reaching the specific objectives is not easily measurable.
A call for papers ahead of the conference attracted more than 200 papers. Counting with the the papers from the first conference, the organisers currently have a total of 42 high quality papers, meaning that significant content has been produced, but the challenge of curating and publishing them remains.
The final report produced by the consortium members reflects positive feedback from participants who particularly appreciated the learning coming out of the conference and the nonacademic bias which allowed for both scholars and practitioners to share perspectives of the state of democracy. Participants also noted the diversity of topics and that the conference featured a significant number of up-and-coming democratic activists and researchers.
Among the concrete outputs are a conference statement on regalvanizing democracy in Africa and an Elders retreat 2023 Communiqué.
Apart from these rather isolated outcomes, the Embassy has not been able to identify more substantial results.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
